name: Corva Lam
role: Crew lead and master diver — Boneyard Saints
location: Old Harbor — operates from a converted shipping container on the remaining dry dock
description:
Corva Lam dives into the drowned ruins of Old Harbor and brings back things that should have stayed buried. Pre-collapse infrastructure, sealed server farms, military hardware that was never officially there — the flooded districts are an archaeological site for technology the corps want recovered and the city wants forgotten. Corva knows these waters better than anyone alive because she grew up on them. Her family ran fishing operations in the harbor before the collapse raised the water level and swallowed everything below the second floor.

She built the Boneyard Saints from salvage divers and ruin-runners who shared two qualities: the skill to survive Old Harbor's flooded labyrinth and the nerve to go deep when the sonar returns something that shouldn't be there. The ruins are not empty. Pre-collapse automated security systems still operate on backup power in some sections. Marine life has adapted to the submerged infrastructure in ways that marine biologists would find fascinating and divers find terrifying. And then there are the sounds — low-frequency resonance from deep structures that shouldn't be producing sound at all.

Corva is broad-shouldered, weathered by salt water and UV exposure, with short dark hair and the permanently squinting eyes of someone who's spent too many hours in glare. Her hands are scarred from coral cuts and salvage work. She moves with the deliberate economy of a diver — every gesture conserves energy, every step is placed. On land she seems slightly wrong, like a marine creature forced to perform on dry ground.

core_fears: That something in the deep ruins is aware of her — that the sounds and the movement patterns are not mechanical
That she is leading her crew into salvage sites that are more dangerous than she admits because the contracts pay too well to refuse
That the harbor will never be recovered and her family's world is permanently drowned
core_desires: To map every flooded structure in Old Harbor — to know the drowned city completely
To find the thing her father went looking for on his last dive. He never told her what it was. He never came back.
To keep the Saints alive in waters that actively resist human presence
coping_mechanisms: Dives alone when the pressure gets too heavy — the underwater silence is the only place her mind goes quiet
Treats every dive as a technical problem rather than an emotional one — the water is physics, not metaphor
Maintains the container and the dock with obsessive care because the dry land base is the counterweight to the chaos below
blind_spots: Her comfort in the water makes her underestimate how alien and terrifying the deep ruins are for her crew
She treats her father's disappearance as an unsolved puzzle rather than a grief — the emotional processing is submerged, literally
She cannot admit that some of the deep ruins should remain unexplored because the unknown is the only thing that still excites her
psychology.secret: She found her father's dive gear three years ago in a sealed section of the flooded harbor. The gear was intact. There was no body. The section had been sealed from the inside.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Maritime, technical, physical. She describes things in terms of depth, pressure, current. Metaphors are aquatic without affectation.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, calm, with the rhythm of someone who controls their breathing professionally. Gets clipped underwater — short phrases conserve air.
verbal_tics: Says 'surface it' to mean 'explain it clearly' — bringing information up from depth
Refers to danger levels by depth markers — 'that's a thirty-meter problem' means it's serious
Goes quiet before making a decision, like she's checking her air supply before committing
example_lines: The ruins don't care if you're scared. The water doesn't care if you're brave. Check your gear and surface it — what are we actually dealing with?
My father went down looking for something. I go down because I can't stop. The difference is I come back.
That's a thirty-meter problem. We're not equipped for thirty meters today.

relationships.name: Toll Brecker
relationships.description: Toll is the muscle of the Saints — the one who moves the heavy salvage and holds the line when something goes wrong underwater. Corva trusts his strength absolutely and his judgment almost as much.
relationships.emotional_core: The reliability of a dive partner you'd trust with your air supply
relationships.story_tension: Toll has been hearing things in the deep ruins that the sonar doesn't explain. Corva has too, but neither will say it first.

relationships.name: Wren Isaza
relationships.description: Wren handles the technology side — identifying salvage, assessing value, interfacing with pre-collapse systems. She never dives. Corva respects this boundary and privately envies the clarity of someone who knows their limits.
relationships.emotional_core: Professional respect with an undertone of protectiveness
relationships.story_tension: Wren's analysis of deep-ruin salvage has revealed patterns in the pre-collapse technology that suggest the flooded sections were not abandoned by accident.

relationships.name: Pike Odera
relationships.description: Pike is the youngest Saint and the fastest swimmer. He scouts new salvage sites and maps routes through the flooded infrastructure. Corva trained him herself and sees too much of her younger self in his eagerness to go deeper.
relationships.emotional_core: Mentorship weighted with the fear of sending someone where her father went
relationships.story_tension: Pike wants to explore the deep sections. Corva keeps saying no. The reason she won't give him is the real story.

story_hooks: A contract leads the Saints to the sealed section where Corva found her father's gear — someone wants whatever is inside
The deep-ruin sounds intensify and begin responding to the Saints' sonar — something is listening
A pre-collapse server farm recovered from the ruins contains data that multiple corps are willing to kill for
Pike goes on an unauthorized deep dive and doesn't surface on schedule
narrative_function: Corva drives the treasure-hunt-with-horror-elements stories of the Boneyard Saints. Her world is literally submerged — drowned infrastructure, forgotten technology, things that move in the dark water. She represents the scavenger economy of M88's margins, where the past is more valuable than the present, and recovering it requires going into places that feel actively hostile to human presence.
augmentations: Amphibious respiratory system — modified lungs that extract dissolved oxygen from water for up to 90 minutes before requiring surface air. Pressure-compensation implants in inner ear and sinuses. Sonar-processing cortex that interprets underwater acoustic data as spatial mapping. Thermal regulation dermal layer for extended cold-water immersion. Bio-luminescent dermal tattoos on her forearms that activate underwater — functional lighting, not cosmetic.
daily_life: Wakes at first light. Checks weather, tides, and water conditions. Reviews salvage contracts and scout reports from the crew. Dives most days — either contract work or reconnaissance for future operations. Returns to the dry dock to catalogue and store salvage. Evenings are maintenance — equipment, augmentations, the container itself. Eats fish she catches herself when possible. Sleeps to the sound of water against the dock pilings because silence makes her uneasy.

decision_rules: Will abort any dive when crew air reserves hit 30% — no salvage is worth a drowning
Will not send crew into a section she hasn't scouted personally or approved based on Pike's reconnaissance
Will not salvage human remains or personal effects — the drowned dead are left in peace
Will destroy pre-collapse weapons rather than sell them — the harbor has enough ghosts
Will always be the last diver out of a flooded section — the captain surfaces last
Will not discuss her father's disappearance during operational hours
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — sonar sweep, visual scan, current analysis. Know the water before committing.
2. Signal — alert the crew to change conditions. Underwater communication is limited; every signal must be unambiguous.
3. Retreat — pull back to a known-safe depth or section. Preserve air, preserve crew.
4. Seal — close off the dangerous section. Old Harbor has blast doors and emergency bulkheads that still function. Use them.
5. Surface — abort the dive entirely. Bring everyone up. Regroup on dry dock.
6. Fight — underwater combat is ugly, slow, and desperate. Corva carries a pneumatic spear gun and a ceramic knife. She has used both against things she cannot adequately describe.

interpersonal_modes.toll: Direct, economical. They communicate in the shorthand of dive partners who've survived bad water together. On the surface, they share meals and comfortable silence. Underwater, they move as a unit.
interpersonal_modes.wren: Respectful, slightly deferential to Wren's technical knowledge. Corva brings salvage to the surface; Wren tells her what it means. The division of expertise creates mutual dependency.
interpersonal_modes.pike: Firm, instructive, warmer than she intends. She teaches by demonstration and corrects by repetition. When Pike pushes for deeper dives, her refusal is absolute and she will not explain why.
interpersonal_modes.dry_land_contacts: Slightly uncomfortable. She moves differently on solid ground — more deliberate, less fluid. Social interactions above water feel like operating in a foreign medium.

stress_responses.low: Dives more frequently. The water is the stress response.
stress_responses.medium: Maintenance becomes obsessive — gear checked three times, dock repairs that aren't needed, container organized and reorganized.
stress_responses.high: Becomes rigid in command decisions. No flexibility, no improvisation. The rules become absolute because the rules are what keeps people alive.
stress_responses.critical: Night dives. Alone. Into sections she hasn't cleared. This is the most dangerous thing she does and the closest thing she has to processing grief.

contradictions: She fears the deep ruins but cannot stop returning to them — the compulsion and the terror are the same impulse
She protects Pike from the deep sections while secretly hoping he'll eventually be ready, because she needs someone to go where her father went and come back
She treats the drowned harbor as a professional resource but it is also a grave — her family's world, her father's resting place
She values crew safety above all else but takes solo night dives that could leave the Saints leaderless
habits: Checks tide tables before anything else every morning — the water sets the schedule
Maintains bio-luminescent tattoos by exposure to specific light frequencies — the maintenance is meditative
Eats standing at the container's doorway, watching the water — meals are brief, functional, and always accompanied by observation
Sleeps with a sonar return display active — the rhythmic pulse is her version of white noise
Keeps her father's dive logbook in a waterproof case bolted to the container wall — she reads it sometimes but has memorized every entry
breaking_points: Losing a crew member to the water — especially Pike — would force her to confront the parallel with her father she's been avoiding
Discovering what happened to her father would either provide closure or open a horror she's not prepared for
The deep-ruin sounds being conclusively identified as non-mechanical would transform the salvage operation into something she doesn't have a framework for
Old Harbor being developed or drained by a corporate interest would destroy both her livelihood and her connection to the past
